copyPanel.rule: Mathematical Modeling in Careers & Daily Life
steps: 1. Frame real-world problems mathematically using rates, percentages, and geometry
2. Collect and analyze data to optimize decisions and resource allocation
3. Communicate quantitative findings clearly with equations and visual models

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Brushing Your Teeth
revealWordProblem.text:
For good hygiene you should brush your teeth twice a day. Leaving the water running while you brush wastes an average of four gallons, compared with turning the water on only to rinse.
Question: How much water would you save each year if every person in your house ran the water only to rinse? How does your saving compare with a household of 3, 4, 5, and 8 people?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: Five toothbrushes in a row, each a different color.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Each brushing saves about 4 gallons, and you brush twice a day, so one person saves 8 gallons a day. In a year that is 8 × 365 = 2,920 gallons per person. Multiply by the number of people: 3 people save 8,760 gallons, 4 people save 11,680 gallons, 5 people save 14,600 gallons, and 8 people save 23,360 gallons. Every extra person in the house adds another 2,920 gallons saved.

questions.stem: A planter is 4 feet long and 2 feet wide. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Area of a rectangle is length × width: 4 × 2 = 8 square feet.
choiceFeedback: 6 comes from adding 4 + 2 instead of multiplying.
12 comes from adding all four sides (4 + 2 + 4 + 2) — that is the perimeter, not the area.
2 comes from dividing 4 by 2 instead of multiplying.
hints: Area tells how much flat space the planter covers.
For a rectangle, multiply length by width.
Multiply 4 × 2.
questions.stemEs: Una jardinera mide 4 pies de largo y 2 pies de ancho. ¿Cuál es su área?
questions.explanationEs: El área de un rectángulo es largo × ancho: 4 × 2 = 8 pies cuadrados.
hintsEs: El área dice cuánto espacio plano cubre la jardinera.
Para un rectángulo, multiplica largo por ancho.
Multiplica 4 × 2.

questions.stem: That same planter is 4 feet long, 2 feet wide, and needs soil 1 foot deep. How much soil does the gardener need?
questions.explanation: Volume is length × width × depth: 4 × 2 × 1 = 8 cubic feet of soil.
choiceFeedback: 7 comes from adding 4 + 2 + 1 instead of multiplying.
The number is right but soil fills space, so volume needs cubic units, not square units.
4 forgets to multiply by the width of 2.
hints: Soil fills space, so you need volume.
Volume of a box is length × width × depth.
Multiply 4 × 2 × 1.
questions.stemEs: Esa misma jardinera mide 4 pies de largo, 2 pies de ancho y necesita tierra de 1 pie de profundidad. ¿Cuánta tierra necesita el jardinero?
questions.explanationEs: El volumen es largo × ancho × profundidad: 4 × 2 × 1 = 8 pies cúbicos de tierra.
hintsEs: La tierra llena espacio, así que necesitas el volumen.
El volumen de una caja es largo × ancho × profundidad.
Multiplica 4 × 2 × 1.

questions.stem: Leaving the water running while brushing wastes an average of 4 gallons per brushing. You brush twice a day. How much water can one person save per day by only turning the water on to rinse?
questions.explanation: 4 gallons saved per brushing × 2 brushings a day = 8 gallons a day.
choiceFeedback: 4 gallons is the savings for only ONE brushing — you brush twice a day.
6 comes from adding 4 + 2 instead of multiplying.
2 comes from dividing 4 by 2 instead of multiplying.
hints: How many gallons does one brushing save?
How many times do you brush each day?
Multiply 4 × 2.
questions.stemEs: Dejar el agua corriendo mientras te cepillas desperdicia en promedio 4 galones por cepillado. Te cepillas dos veces al día. ¿Cuánta agua puede ahorrar una persona al día si abre la llave solo para enjuagar?
questions.explanationEs: 4 galones ahorrados por cepillado × 2 cepillados al día = 8 galones al día.
hintsEs: ¿Cuántos galones ahorra un cepillado?
¿Cuántas veces te cepillas al día?
Multiplica 4 × 2.

level1.stem: Which of these is NOT one of the ways chefs use math when planning menus?
choices: Choosing the color of the restaurant's walls
Calculating the price point for each item
Deciding on the portion size of each item
Projecting how much food is needed for each day

level2.stem: One person saves 8 gallons of water a day by turning the water on only to rinse. How much water does that person save in a year (365 days)?
level2.explanation: 8 gallons a day × 365 days = 2,920 gallons in a year.
choiceFeedback: 373 comes from adding 8 + 365 instead of multiplying.
1,460 multiplies 365 by 4 — the savings from one brushing — instead of the full 8 gallons a day.
365 is just the number of days; it forgets to multiply by the gallons saved each day.
hints: You know the savings per day.
How many days are in a year?
Multiply 8 × 365.
level2.stemEs: Una persona ahorra 8 galones de agua al día al abrir la llave solo para enjuagar. ¿Cuánta agua ahorra esa persona en un año (365 días)?
level2.explanationEs: 8 galones al día × 365 días = 2,920 galones en un año.
hintsEs: Conoces el ahorro por día.
¿Cuántos días tiene un año?
Multiplica 8 × 365.

level2.stem: If each person in a house saves 2,920 gallons a year, how much does a household of 3 people save in a year?
level2.explanation: 2,920 gallons per person × 3 people = 8,760 gallons a year.
choiceFeedback: 2,923 comes from adding 2,920 + 3 instead of multiplying.
973 (about 2,920 ÷ 3) divides instead of multiplying — more people save MORE water, not less.
5,840 multiplies by 2 people instead of 3.
hints: Each person saves the same amount.
3 people, each saving 2,920 gallons.
Multiply 2,920 × 3.
level2.stemEs: Si cada persona de una casa ahorra 2,920 galones al año, ¿cuánto ahorra en un año un hogar de 3 personas?
level2.explanationEs: 2,920 galones por persona × 3 personas = 8,760 galones al año.
hintsEs: Cada persona ahorra la misma cantidad.
3 personas, cada una ahorrando 2,920 galones.
Multiplica 2,920 × 3.

level2.stem: A household of 5 saves 2,920 gallons per person per year. A household of 4 does the same. How much MORE does the household of 5 save than the household of 4?
level2.explanation: 5 people save 5 × 2,920 = 14,600 gallons and 4 people save 4 × 2,920 = 11,680 gallons. The difference is 14,600 − 11,680 = 2,920 gallons — exactly one more person's savings.
choiceFeedback: 14,600 is the TOTAL for the household of 5, not the difference between the two households.
11,680 is the TOTAL for the household of 4, not the difference between the two households.
1 is just the difference in the number of people — each of those people saves 2,920 gallons.
hints: How many more people does the bigger household have?
One more person means one more person's yearly savings.
Each person saves 2,920 gallons a year.
level2.stemEs: Un hogar de 5 personas ahorra 2,920 galones por persona al año. Un hogar de 4 hace lo mismo. ¿Cuánto MÁS ahorra el hogar de 5 que el de 4?
level2.explanationEs: 5 personas ahorran 5 × 2,920 = 14,600 galones y 4 personas ahorran 4 × 2,920 = 11,680 galones. La diferencia es 14,600 − 11,680 = 2,920 galones — exactamente el ahorro de una persona más.
hintsEs: ¿Cuántas personas más tiene el hogar más grande?
Una persona más significa el ahorro anual de una persona más.
Cada persona ahorra 2,920 galones al año.

level2.stem: Choose another person who works in a restaurant — not the chef — and describe the math they would use.
level2.modelAnswer: A server uses math all shift. They add up each table's bill, calculate the change for customers paying cash, and figure out their tips as a percent of each check. At the end of the night they total their tips to see what they earned.
sentenceStems: A ___ in a restaurant uses math when ___ .
level2.stemEs: Escoge otra persona que trabaje en un restaurante — que no sea el chef — y describe las matemáticas que usaría.

level2.stem: A gardener's planter has an area of 8 square feet, and each plant needs 2 square feet of space to grow. How many plants fit in the planter?
level2.explanation: 8 square feet ÷ 2 square feet per plant = 4 plants.
choiceFeedback: 16 multiplies 8 × 2 instead of dividing — that would need a much bigger planter.
10 comes from adding 8 + 2 instead of dividing.
6 comes from subtracting 8 − 2 instead of dividing.
hints: You are splitting the area into equal shares of space.
How many groups of 2 square feet fit inside 8 square feet?
Divide 8 by 2.
level2.stemEs: La jardinera de un jardinero tiene un área de 8 pies cuadrados, y cada planta necesita 2 pies cuadrados de espacio para crecer. ¿Cuántas plantas caben en la jardinera?
level2.explanationEs: 8 pies cuadrados ÷ 2 pies cuadrados por planta = 4 plantas.
hintsEs: Estás repartiendo el área en partes iguales de espacio.
¿Cuántos grupos de 2 pies cuadrados caben en 8 pies cuadrados?
Divide 8 entre 2.

level2.stem: What factors do you consider to determine the number of plants you can put in a planter garden? Is the TYPE of plant a factor? Explain your thinking.
level2.modelAnswer: I would consider the area of the planter and how much space each plant needs between it and its neighbors. The type of plant is definitely a factor, because a tomato plant needs much more space than a radish — so the same 8-square-foot planter could hold many radishes but only a few tomato plants.
sentenceStems: The type of plant matters because ___ .
level2.stemEs: ¿Qué factores consideras para determinar cuántas plantas puedes poner en una jardinera? ¿El TIPO de planta es un factor? Explica tu razonamiento.

Those add the household size to 2,920 instead of multiplying by it.
46,720 is 16 × 2,920 — that doubles the 8-person household instead of computing it.
hints: Each household total is people × 2,920.

level3.stemEs: Cada persona ahorra 2,920 galones al año. ¿Cuál compara correctamente hogares de 3, 4, 5 y 8 personas?

level3.stem: Someone says, 'Math is just a school subject. I'll never use it after class.' Using the chef, the gardener, or the water problem, write what you would say back.
level3.modelAnswer: I would say that a chef never stops using math — they calculate prices, portion sizes, and how much of each ingredient to order every single day. Even at home, math showed us that one person who turns off the tap while brushing saves 2,920 gallons a year. You do not escape math after class; you just stop noticing you are using it.
level3.stemEs: Alguien dice: 'Las matemáticas son solo una materia escolar. Nunca las usaré fuera de clase.' Usando al chef, al jardinero o el problema del agua, escribe qué le responderías.

level3.stem: A chef expects 120 customers tonight and projects that 1 out of every 4 will order the soup. Each serving of soup uses 2 cups of broth. How much broth should the chef prepare?
level3.explanation: 120 ÷ 4 = 30 soup orders, and 30 orders × 2 cups each = 60 cups of broth.
choiceFeedback: 240 uses all 120 customers × 2 cups — but only 1 in 4 customers orders the soup.
30 is the number of soup ORDERS; it forgets to multiply by the 2 cups each serving needs.
15 divides the 30 orders by 2 instead of multiplying by 2.
hints: First find how many customers will order soup.
120 ÷ 4 = 30 orders.
Now, how many cups do 30 servings need?
level3.stemEs: Un chef espera 120 clientes esta noche y calcula que 1 de cada 4 pedirá la sopa. Cada porción de sopa usa 2 tazas de caldo. ¿Cuánto caldo debe preparar el chef?
level3.explanationEs: 120 ÷ 4 = 30 órdenes de sopa, y 30 órdenes × 2 tazas cada una = 60 tazas de caldo.
hintsEs: Halla primero cuántos clientes pedirán sopa.
120 ÷ 4 = 30 órdenes.
Ahora, ¿cuántas tazas necesitan 30 porciones?

level3.stem: Pick a hobby — yours or anyone's — and list at least three specific math tasks hiding inside it, the way the lesson did for gardening.
level3.modelAnswer: In skateboarding: you measure the height and length of a ramp to know if you can clear it, you count how many tries a trick takes and track whether that number is going down, and you estimate speed and distance before a gap so you know how hard to push. The board itself is measured in inches, and riders compare deck widths like 8.0 versus 8.25.
